items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: That was our record, and then they gave me a tune by the name of 'Changes,' a Walter Donaldson tune, awfully nice.

ctx.x: So I just figured I'd get a little jazz band in there somewhere on the record, so I had Jimmy, Tommy and I didn't have a piano -- Jimmy, Tommy and Steve and Bix and they played the part. They just played just a chorus or so and then we went back to Hoagy's singing, and geez, it worked out well.
That was our record, and then they gave me a tune by the name of "Changes," a Walter Donaldson tune, awfully nice.

It turned out well. I used all the voices in there. I went to Paul and asked him, I said, 'What do I use or what don't I use?' 'Use whatever you want.' So boy I did. I had everybody and I had the 'sweet' trio, 'sweet' in quotes and that is Johnny Fulton, Skin Young and Charlie Gaylord and then I put let's see, I put Rinker in with them because he could sing a falsetto and I had Bing sing -- he sang the patter.
